rationale: This is the archive's gen-0 winner with the winsorization swapped for a capped denominator — the same numerator, same deflator and same hypothesis — so it is a scaling variant rather than a new mechanism, and the cap will pile a large mass of firms at exactly ±1, making the extreme portfolios degenerate ties rather than more stable.

Multiplying signed PPE growth by a non-negative [0,1] accrual rank means the long leg is populated by high-accrual firms with contracting fixed capital, which directly contradicts the accrual mechanism the signal is supposed to exploit (and contradicts the sister proposal AccrualBloatWithoutCapitalReplacement), so the expected sign is not cleanly implied by the expression.

The rank-product of balance-sheet accrual intensity and sub-replacement capx/dp is a coherent, non-cancelling intersection that tests the opposite gate direction from the archive's failed CapexWeightedByAccrualQuality, making it a substantive diagnosis-driven follow-up rather than a cosmetic variant.

The claim that neither leg carries a cross-sectional premium is wrong — TS_RANK(capx/at) is essentially abnormal capital investment (Titman-Wei-Xie), whose documented direction implies low recent capex predicts *high* returns, so the capex leg pushes against the stated negative expected sign and only the working-capital leg supports it.

Decomposing the winner's numerator into the reversal-prone receivable/inventory channel is a legitimate mechanism refinement with correct recch/invch sign handling, though it inherits the ±1 mass-point problem of the capped deflator and the post-1988 coverage loss could easily make any improvement a sparse-sample artifact.

Both legs are individually well-documented return predictors in the same direction (Sloan accruals and Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan net external financing), so the rank product will largely load additively on two known anomalies; without orthogonalizing to the component ranks the test cannot show any incremental interaction effect.
